IV. ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF THE PROJECT

General
This proposed freeway facility will be accessible at the interchange locations provided at I-94, the airport entrance road, the new air cargo area and Howell Avenue. Since this freeway will be in an embankment section for most of its length, the local through streets will be bridged, thereby allowing local community circulation to continue practically unimpaired. Local fire and health protection, bussing of school children, access to churches, and private enterprise services routes will not be interrupted. Travel over the local street system will operate more efficiently, for the new facility is designed to attract airport oriented traffic.
Gne hundred twenty persons attended a Location Public
Hearing on March 25, 1969. Testimony revealed that the Milwaukee
County Board, Milwaukee Common Council, SEWRPC, Federal Aviation
Administration and the American Automobile Association favored construction of the Airport Spur. Milwaukee County's Park Commission indicated
that the proposed facility did not interfere with any existing or
proposed park development. A spokesman for the Milwaukee School
Board neither endorsed nor condemned the Airport Spur but was concerned
with the effect of housing acquisition for Mitchell Field's Air Cargo
Area on Hamlin Garland School. The private citizens that testified\nexpressed concern only on the financing of the project.
